Scatter/line chart with x-axis: "GDP per capita relative to the frontier (United States) (%)" from 0 to 100, and y-axis: "Annual growth in GDP per capita (%)" from 0 to 7. The figure shows multiple country trajectories connecting projected recent-history points, with a legend for Argentina, Bangladesh, Bulgaria, Chile, China, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Poland, and Türkiye. Solid lines indicate countries that will experience convergence to the frontier over 2023–2100; dashed lines indicate countries that will experience divergence from the frontier over 2023–2100, although they were closer to the frontier in 2022. Visible patterns: Poland is a long solid teal line extending from roughly the mid-20s percent of US GDP per capita to 100%, with growth easing from a little above 5% to about 3.3–3.8%; China is a solid orange-red line extending from roughly the low-20s to the low-60s, with growth around 5% falling to around 2–3%; India is a solid brown/orange line around the low single digits to the mid-20s, flattening near 3.8%; Bangladesh is a solid olive line from very low frontier proximity to the high-20s, falling from above 6% toward about 3%; Indonesia is a solid blue line from the high single digits to the high-20s, settling near 3%; Türkiye is a solid gray line from the mid-20s to low-30s, near 2%; Argentina, Chile, Mexico, and Bulgaria are dashed trajectories rising from low frontier proximity into the mid-teens to low-20s while growth rises sharply from near 0–1% to around 1.5–3%.
